quick_facts.one_line: JWT-based login with role-based access control for all five staff roles.
quick_facts.status_reason: Sprint 1 complete. JWT auth + RBAC fully implemented, 11 tests green, build passing.

content.title: Authentication & RBAC
content.tldr: Users log in with email + password. Server issues a JWT access token (15 min) and a refresh token (7 days). All endpoints are protected by JwtAuthGuard and RolesGuard. Five roles: admin, store-manager, cashier, accountant, viewer.
content.summary: This module implements the full authentication lifecycle: user registration (admin only), login, token refresh, and logout. RBAC is enforced at the controller level using a @Roles() decorator backed by a RolesGuard. All passwords are bcrypt-hashed. Refresh tokens are stored in Redis with TTL matching the 7-day expiry.

skip_if.description: Conditions under which agents should NOT read this file
conditions: You are working on product, order, or invoice features and only need to know the User entity shape — read entity-registry.json instead
You need the API contract shape — read api-contracts/auth.json directly

do_not: Do NOT store refresh tokens in PostgreSQL — use Redis only
Do NOT allow self-registration — only admin can create users
Do NOT skip RolesGuard on any mutating endpoint
Do NOT return passwordHash in any API response

items.i_want: to create a new staff account with an assigned role and store
items.so_that: new employees can log in and access only their permitted functions
acceptance_criteria: Given valid email, password, role, storeId — When POST /api/v1/users is called by admin — Then 201 is returned with user object (id, email, role, storeId, isActive, createdAt), passwordHash omitted
Given an email already in use — When POST /api/v1/users is called — Then 409 Conflict with message 'Email already registered'
Given a role not in [admin, store-manager, cashier, accountant, viewer] — When POST /api/v1/users is called — Then 400 Bad Request with validation message
Given caller is not admin — When POST /api/v1/users is called — Then 403 Forbidden
Given password shorter than 8 characters — When POST /api/v1/users is called — Then 400 Bad Request 'Password must be at least 8 characters'
edge_cases: storeId references a non-existent store — 400 Bad Request
storeId references a deactivated store — 400 Bad Request 'Store is not active'
business_rules: Password is bcrypt-hashed at cost 12 before storage
passwordHash is NEVER returned in any response
isActive defaults to true on creation

items.as_a: any Staff Member (bất kỳ nhân viên nào)
items.i_want: to log in with my email and password
items.so_that: I receive a JWT access token and refresh token to use the system
acceptance_criteria: Given valid credentials — When POST /api/v1/auth/login — Then 200 with { accessToken, refreshToken, user: { id, email, role, storeId } }
Given wrong password — When POST /api/v1/auth/login — Then 401 with generic message 'Invalid credentials' (no enumeration)
Given unknown email — When POST /api/v1/auth/login — Then 401 with same generic message 'Invalid credentials'
Given isActive=false user — When POST /api/v1/auth/login — Then 401 'Account is deactivated'
Given user whose store has isActive=false — When POST /api/v1/auth/login — Then 401 'Store is deactivated'
Given valid login — Then accessToken payload contains { sub: userId, email, role, storeId, iat, exp }
Given valid login — Then refreshToken is stored in Redis with key refresh:{userId} and TTL 604800s
edge_cases: Rapid repeated failed logins — rate limiter returns 429 after 10 attempts in 1 minute
User logs in from two devices — both refresh tokens should coexist (keyed by userId:deviceId or replace strategy — see business rule)
Email submitted in mixed case (e.g. 'User@Store.vn') — normalised toLower before lookup
business_rules: Emails are stored and compared as lowercase
Same error message for wrong password and unknown email — prevents user enumeration (OWASP)
Refresh token for the same user:device pair overwrites the previous one in Redis (single-session per device strategy for Sprint 1)

items.i_want: to exchange my refresh token for a new access token
items.so_that: I stay logged in during my shift without entering my password again
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid, non-expired refresh token present in Redis — When POST /api/v1/auth/refresh — Then 200 with { accessToken, refreshToken }
Given a refresh token not found in Redis (expired or already rotated) — When POST /api/v1/auth/refresh — Then 401 'Invalid or expired refresh token'
Given a valid refresh — Then old refresh token is deleted from Redis and new one is stored (token rotation)
Given a valid refresh — Then new accessToken has a fresh exp (iat + 900s)
edge_cases: An attacker replays an already-rotated refresh token — returns 401 (token no longer in Redis)
Refresh called 1 second before Redis TTL expiry — still valid if key exists in Redis
business_rules: Token rotation is mandatory — reuse of a rotated refresh token = 401
New refresh token TTL resets to 604800s on every successful refresh

items.so_that: my session is immediately invalidated and my device cannot be used by someone else
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid access token — When POST /api/v1/auth/logout — Then 200 OK and refresh token is deleted from Redis
Given refresh token not in Redis (already logged out) — When POST /api/v1/auth/logout — Then 200 OK (idempotent, no error)
Given no Authorization header — When POST /api/v1/auth/logout — Then 401
edge_cases: User logs out on device A — device B's refresh token is NOT affected (per-device isolation in Sprint 1 single-session model)
business_rules: Logout must be idempotent — second logout of same token returns 200, not 404
Access tokens cannot be revoked mid-TTL in Sprint 1 (short 15-min window is accepted risk — token blacklist is deferred)

items.so_that: a departing employee immediately loses all access
acceptance_criteria: Given a valid userId — When PATCH /api/v1/users/:id/deactivate by admin — Then 200 and user.isActive=false
Given the user is already inactive — When PATCH /api/v1/users/:id/deactivate — Then 200 (idempotent)
Given caller is not admin — When PATCH /api/v1/users/:id/deactivate — Then 403
Given userId does not exist — When PATCH /api/v1/users/:id/deactivate — Then 404
Given user is deactivated — When that user's refresh token is used — Then 401 'Account is deactivated'
edge_cases: Admin deactivates themselves — allowed (system allows it, operational risk is documented)
Deactivated user's existing access token: still valid for up to 15 min remaining TTL — accepted risk in Sprint 1, blacklisting deferred
business_rules: Deactivation is soft-delete only — isActive=false, no row deletion
Deactivated user's Redis refresh token is deleted immediately on deactivation
Reactivation (isActive=true) is a separate PATCH /api/v1/users/:id/reactivate endpoint — admin only

items.so_that: I can confirm my role and store assignment
acceptance_criteria: Given valid JWT — When GET /api/v1/auth/me — Then 200 with { id, email, role, storeId, isActive, createdAt }
Given no/invalid JWT — When GET /api/v1/auth/me — Then 401
business_rules: passwordHash is NEVER included in this response

sections.heading: Business Rules — Consolidated
items: BR-AUTH-01: Passwords minimum 8 characters, bcrypt cost 12
BR-AUTH-02: Emails stored and compared as lowercase — normalise on create and login
BR-AUTH-03: Access token TTL = 900s (15 min); payload: { sub, email, role, storeId }
BR-AUTH-04: Refresh token TTL = 604800s (7 days); stored in Redis key refresh:{userId}
BR-AUTH-05: Token rotation — every /auth/refresh invalidates old token and issues new
BR-AUTH-06: Deactivated user login → 401; their Redis refresh token deleted immediately
BR-AUTH-07: Deactivated store login → 401 for ALL users of that store
BR-AUTH-08: No user enumeration — same 401 message for wrong password and unknown email
BR-AUTH-09: passwordHash never exposed in any API response
BR-AUTH-10: Rate limit on /auth/login — 10 attempts per minute per IP → 429

sections.heading: RBAC Matrix
sections.note: ❌ = 403 Forbidden if called by that role. Future endpoint permissions defined in api-contracts/auth.json.

items.question: Should admin be able to force-expire another user's active access token (blacklist)?
items.default_decision: No — 15-min TTL is accepted risk for Sprint 1

items.question: Multi-device login — should a user have one refresh token per device or one global?
items.decision: One per user (global) for Sprint 1. Per-device keying deferred.

items.question: Password reset flow — how does a user recover a forgotten password?
items.default_decision: Admin resets manually (PATCH /users/:id/reset-password) until email service is set up
